configs.description: The switch as shipped: 24 non-PoE ports, the built-in AC power supply and one built-in front-to-back fan. EX4000-24T is the only hardware SKU the datasheet lists for the model (Table 1 and the ordering information); there is no DC, back-to-front, -S or -TAA variant.
configs.name: ac

gaps.wanted: The brackets of EX-RMK (provided), EX-4PST-RMK and JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (orderable) are named in Table 5 and the mounting topics and are not modelled as kit contracts in this slice. A dimensioned drawing of the bracket fold lines would give the flush position an at.

A per-port vocabulary for the Status lamp. Table 32 gives its colour by speed (off 10 Mbps, blinking green 100 Mbps, green 1000 Mbps, amber 2.5 Gbps), which the jack's own lamp states do not carry, so the jack keeps the component's default off, link and activity states.
The size of the claim code label (Figure 11 callout 6). It is drawn as a region and not as a part, and the photograph does not show it.
The Junos interface names. The hardware guide gives the PIC numbering only inside the Junos configuration topics, which this slice does not read.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.
The diameter and depth of the pinhole reset button (Figure 11 callout 5). The guide names the button and gives no size; the hole is drawn at 2.0 mm as an estimate.
an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on port group rj45 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: Table 16, Figure 28 and the cooling section - front to back (air out), the fan at the rear. The datasheet gives 9 CFM.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Table 16 and Table 17 - the switch has an internal power supply (fixed PSU) and one inbuilt fan with front-to-back airflow; the guide's system overview says the EX4000 switch models have inbuilt fixed fans and power supply units. The guide gives no replacement procedure for either, and no part number. They are part of the chassis and not bays and not components.

chassis.note: Table 17 and Table 26 - height 1.71 in (4.34 cm), width 17.36 in (44.10 cm), depth 8.43 in (21.40 cm), weight 6.3 lb (2.9 kg). The datasheet gives the same width and height, a depth of 8.42 in (21.40 cm) and a system weight of 2.89 kg; the guide's inches are carried through their centimetre figure, 214.0 mm. The width of 441.0 mm is the metal between the bracket fold lines: the photograph shows no ears and the jack pitch closes on the registry at that width.

color.note: median of the bare face left of the first jack shell in the front photograph, #7d838e. Sampled from a studio photograph, whose white balance may differ from the metal. The numerals are the photograph's white, #e4e6e9.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The drawing and the photograph agree on what is on the face. The photograph prints the port numbers in white on this non-PoE model, the drawing in black, and prints only EX4000 as the model legend. The drawing draws a round lamp before each of SYS, MST and CLD where the photograph shows none. The photograph of the real device wins for the lettering and the drawing for the lamps. The Juniper logo and the driven by Mist AI line are not drawn: a logo-zone is reserved.

ears.note: The guide's quick-start topic says the two-post rack mounting kit EX-RMK (Table 5, provided) ships in the box with brackets that bolt flush with the front, and the mounting topics give a 2 in. recessed position with the 2-in. recessed front-mounting brackets of the four-post kit EX-4PST-RMK (Table 5, orderable; also a flush four-post mount). The enhanced toolless four-post kit JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (orderable) is a further kit. The recess is 2 in. (50.8 mm). No figure measures a bracket fold line, so only the recess has an at (the flush at: 0 is the datum of the face), and the kits are not listed under kits in this slice: they are named here and not modelled as kind kit contracts.

earthing.note: The Connect to Power topic and Figure 12 - a two-hole protective earthing terminal on the rear panel, secured with two M5 x 10 mm screws with washers (not supplied) and a lug on 6 AWG wire. The holes are drawn as decor.

front-layout.note: estimated - Figure 11 and the front photograph. The face is the EX4000-24P's: 24 jacks in two shells of six columns and two rows, the first cell at 178.4 mm and the column pitch 13.97 mm, the shells 10.1 mm further apart than the jacks (a gap of about 6 mm), the rows 14.3 mm apart with the upper row turned 180 so that its latch and lamps face up. The two SFP+ columns, the status pill, the USB port and the reset pinhole sit where the 24P has them, checked by overlay. The plain left half carries the model legend and slot-vent strips along the top and bottom edges.

guide-faces.note: The guide has flat drawings of the front (Figure 11) and rear (Figure 12) and no top, bottom or side elevations; the isometric views are not used.

port-lamps.note: Figures 22 to 26 and Tables 32 and 33 - each RJ-45 jack has a Link Activity lamp at one corner and a Status lamp at the other; the common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 housing carries both. Each SFP+ port has a Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp, the triangles in the band between the two cage rows. The order down, up, down, up across a column is the EX4100's (down arrows for the lower port, up arrows for the upper one); the guide does not say which triangle is which lamp, so that order is estimated. The Status lamp's colour shows speed (Table 32), so its states are not expressible as one vocabulary here (see gaps).

port-numbering.note: The photograph and Figure 11 print 0 and 1, 2 and 3, up to 22 and 23 under the column pairs, each number followed by its triangle (an up triangle after the even number and a down triangle after the odd one), so the upper jack of a column is the even port. The numbers are white on this non-PoE model, orange on the PoE models. The four SFP+ cages are printed 0 and 1 inside a rounded outline (the Virtual Chassis ports) and 2 and 3 outside it (the uplink ports). Port numbers are as printed on the metal, from 0. The guide gives no interface names, so none is recorded.

power.note: Table 34 - input 100 to 240 VAC at 1.5 A, 50 to 60 Hz. The datasheet's Table 2 gives a maximum system power consumption of 43 W with no PoE. The guide's PoE budget table (Table 35) has no row for the non-PoE models. The cord is a C13 coupler (power cord topic).

rear.note: estimated - Figure 12 and the rear photograph. From the left: the RJ-45 management port over the RJ-45 console port in one housing, printed MGMT and CON with a triangle each, a lighter plate with the two-hole protective earthing terminal and the earth symbol, one round exhaust fan at the right, a round hole for the power cord retainer (Figure 12 callout 5 is the retainer slot) and the AC inlet in a black housing with its rating printed under it. Five screw heads sit along the lower edge. The fan, earthing and inlet positions are those of the 24P's rear, which the photographs agree with.

scale.note: Gate 1 on the front photograph (2100 x 522 px): the body runs from 110 to 1983 px, 4.25 px/mm, and the jack pitch reads the registry's 13.97 mm ganged pitch to within half a percent. The guide's flat drawing (Figure 11) does not pass: its ports are drawn about 3.5 percent close, so it is used for what is on the face and for the callouts, and the photograph for positions. The rear photograph (2100 x 509 px) runs from 135 to 2003 px and reads at 4.236 px/mm between its own edges.

sources.note: EX4000 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2026-01-20 (261 pages; PDF created 2026-01-20; fetched from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4000/ex4000.pdf, which answered): Table 3 (models), Figure 11 and Figure 12 (the EX4000-24T front and rear panels, flat drawings), Tables 16 and 17 (cooling, power and the physical specifications and ports), Table 26 (chassis), Tables 27 to 33 (the lamps), Table 34 (input), Table 5 (mounting kits) and the mounting topics. EX4000 Line of Ethernet Switches Datasheet, Juniper Networks (PDF created 2025-05-28, 14 pages; https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex4000-line-of-ethernet-switches-datasheet.pdf): Table 1 (the SKUs), Table 2 (maximum system power without PoE), the specifications and the ordering information. Juniper's image-library photographs ex4000-24t-front-high.jpg and ex4000-24t-rear-high.jpg (from https://www.juniper.net/us/en/company/images/image-library-logos-and-product-photos/products/ex4000-24t.html, 2100 px wide, straight on). The guide prints no terms of use; the image-library page prints none either. Nothing of any of them is copied here, since every face is drawn new from measurements. No Visio stencil and no 3D model of the EX4000 is held or published; the intake folder for Juniper EX and QFX was not available to this work and no held photograph, stencil or model was used. End of life was searched on 2026-10-23 and no Juniper notice for the EX4000 was found, so the lifecycle is recorded as none announced.

status-block.note: estimated - Figure 11 callouts 2, 3 and 4 and the photograph. The three chassis lamps SYS, MST and CLD sit in a rounded pill at the top right; the guide's drawing puts a round lamp before each legend and the photograph shows the legends only, so the lamps are drawn 2.6 mm before each legend. Tables 27 to 30 give the lamp meanings; the CLD blink patterns are in another document and are not stated here.

usb-reset.note: estimated - Figure 11 callouts 5 and 7. The USB 2.0 Type-A port with the USB symbol below it and the reset pinhole (callout 5, with the reset symbol below) are read off the photograph. The claim code label (callout 6) is a QR code printed at the right of the face in the drawing and is absent from the photograph, so it is a region and not a part.
